READ THROUGH, AND THEN READ THE NOTE AT THE BOTTOM OF THE GAME.

The idea is certainly captivating, with procedural planets and the power to truly control your own destiny and path and ability to reach the far ends of the universe. At the same time, the implementation can be visually stunning, with the opt for the red of space instead of the blackness that one more commonly associates with the areas void of matter. And I can even forgive the visual glitches, as this machine was by no means meant to game, but has the necessary hardware to run the game on medium settings. 

TL:DR - More ship controls. Vary the Space Stations. More craftable items. More inventory Space. Less crashes. Better Story (Think Skyrim, Hello Games)

Yet then comes the complaints, which are many and varied. Coming into this game, I held as my reference the old games which tried to compete on a smaller scale: Skyrim, Morrowind, and KOTR being the top comparisons. That game had one of the best galaxy systems, and while much smaller than this, managed to incorporate a system of good and evil and overall actions. NMS also does that, by allowing you to build standing in the eyes of various races, which is admirable. But largely, the interaction with these races comes on board nearly identical space station platforms. When I first took off from the planet and ventured abroad, the space stations seemed to be so amazing. But then the next 6 were exactly the same. I understand procedural generation leaving you with not much wiggle room, but at least making the stations bigger. More rooms, more interactions, instead of just one single lonely guy sitting in a chair or standing at a table. And put in more items. More minerals, more rocks and plants, just more. That's what this needs, as crazy as it sounds in a universe of 18000000000000 planets or whatever. More (Actually any) skill trees, more starting inventory space, automated refueling of systems if you have the items. AND MY BIGGEST FAULT WITH THE GAME. Who is GOD'S NAME thought that landing a ship should be "Press E" and not allow the frekaing player any control, really, over where and how the ship sets down. That's the most frustrating and easily fixable thing that the could do. Allow the ship to hover, and allow the user the option to fly close the the ground if they so choose. (Underwater would be nice too)

And don't even get me started on the crashes or the multiplayer aspect...

EDIT: 

THE GAME HAS CHANGED. EVERYTHING THAT WAS WRITTEN BEFORE HAS BEEN CHANGED. 

ABSOLUTELY BUY THIS GAME. EVERYTHING HAS BEEN PROMISED AND MORE.

Update: After Origins patch, the game is still absolutely amazing. I have played most of the space games available today, Space Engineers, Empyrion, Elite Dangerous, X4 Foundations, Star Citizen, and several lesser known titles and No Man's Sky is the only one that has everything that I'm looking for completely and consistently. 

These games are great, don't get me wrong, but all of them are missing things such as "space legs", "titan suits" and things that players want. No Man Sky has them. Build to your hearts content and not with "lego" pieces like some of these space games, real components and building materials.

There is so much to do in game, sometimes its hard to decide what to do as it is all so much fun. You can spend hours one play session just building items, then another few hours exploring amazing planets and moons. Fly around in small ships, drive around in ground vehicles or strap into your exosuit. Then you can teleport or fly to your freighter and build it as your star base or fly to another system to begin exploring all over again. 

Hope you enjoy playing this game as much as I am.

Reviews.222237:
I originally made this review when I was about 30 hours into the game a few days after launch, but as it has been updated and enhanced, I think this game has become something that I can not only enjoy, but completely envelope myself in.

Since I started re-playing it about a year ago, I have enjoyed every minute of it, and I have never felt like I was grinding too much nor spending time on fruitless tasks, The storylines are intricate and complex, but cool at the same time, interlaced with historical lore that, should you choose to learn more about it, opens you up to a universal history of struggle and power.

When the Nexus was introduced into the Space Anomaly, it added an entirely new level of fun and adventure to the game, and it's only gotten better since then, with more exocrafts, planet types, storms, anomalies, and even ships.

There never seems to be an endpoint for me in this game - there is always something to improve upon, always another mission to complete, always another world to discover that's different from the ones I've seen before.

I haven't seen another game that can come close to replicating the open world exploration experience quite like No Man's Sky does. It's truly unique in concept and in practice, and I don't see myself stopping playing it.
